title: Learning Curve vs. Experience Curve
description: Compare the learning curve against the experience curve on a log-scaled production axis and see why one falls faster.
creator: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
Knowledge Systems and Economic Complexity

educational.learningObjective: Given live cost-versus-cumulative-production curves, the learner will compare the learning curve (labor time only) and the experience curve (total unit cost) and explain why the experience curve typically declines faster.
learningOutcomes: Compare the two curves at a given cumulative volume
Explain why the experience curve declines faster
Interpret a logarithmic production axis correctly
educational.assessmentOpportunity: Ask learners to predict both curves' values at a volume not shown, using the doubling rule, then check with the slider.

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Slider playhead across two power-law curves on a log axis
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Controlled comparison - same formula, two retention rates
pedagogical.feedbackType: Both values plus the computed gap at every slider position
misconceptionsAddressed: That the learning curve and the experience curve are the same thing
That cost falls with time rather than with cumulative volume
discussionQuestions: Why does cost fall per doubling rather than per unit?
What happens to the curve when a product is redesigned?
Can an organization buy its way down the experience curve?
